fatal_errors: The proposed as-cast polycrystalline material is fundamentally different from the homogenized, quenched, oriented FCC single crystals used to isolate slip resistance.
Room-temperature testing cannot reveal the target's cryogenic inertial dulling or high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes.

Atomic size mismatch and XRD peak broadening are treated as direct measures of local lattice distortion, although peak width is strongly confounded by grain size, defects, residual stress, and compositional heterogeneity.
The predicted transition to localized or brittle failure is unsupported by the target evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one important part of the target: composition-dependent local lattice distortion can impede dislocation glide and correlate with solid-solution strength. It also proposes a comparative composition series and a nominal falsification rule. However, it reconstructs neither the actual single-crystal CRSS experiment nor its temperature-dependent mechanisms. It omits phonon-drag-controlled inertial motion below roughly 60–77 K, thermally activated glide, strain-rate-jump evidence, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type solute pinning and serrated flow at elevated temperature. Its binary/polycrystalline baseline introduces grain-boundary and compositional confounds, and XRD broadening is not equivalent to the DFT-derived mean-square atomic displacement used in the target correlation. No prior evidence is supplied, despite the prompt explicitly requesting it. Thus it is a broad partial reconstruction of the lattice-distortion strengthening result, not a reconstruction of the full governing-mechanism study.
